rationale: HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED with measurable evidence. Inventory: 16,726 test() calls across 1,838 .test.ts files (~16k claim verified; 16,498 parsed excluding e2e/visual lanes). Granularity: 46.6% of tests contain exactly one expect() call and 71.4% contain <=3 (histogram: 7,680x1, 4,087x2, 2,133x3); median test body is 5 lines. Only 60 of 1,838 files use any .each parametrization today. Verified concrete table-driven candidates: parseDuration in tests/plugins/task-provider-youtrack/helpers.test.ts has 6+ one-line input->output tests; classify-error.test.ts is 63/77 single-expect tests each asserting one error-code mapping; tool-status-labels.test.ts is 42/43 single-expect over pure label formatters; opencode-agent/adapters.test.ts has 110 single-expect cases. These are mechanical test.each consolidations with no behavior risk. SCOPE LIMITS found: (1) 478 files use setupTestDb() and 48 use mock.module() - stateful suites consolidate worse because merged assertions share fixture state and change isolation characteristics; realistic target is the pure-function majority, plausibly 30-50% test-count reduction without touching those. (2) tests/stories/** is byte-for-byte frozen for refactor qualification (docs/architecture/commands.md:47) and must be excluded. (3) Infrastructure coupling: scripts/mutation/baseline.json per-file mutation-score ratchet keys on source-file fingerprints, so consolidated test files shift mutant-kill evidence and need re-baselining awareness; scripts/coverage/floor.json must hold after any deletion; bunfig.toml coverageReporter setup is untouched but coverage is measured over src/+plugins/ so assertion preservation is mandatory. cross_module=true because work spans ~20 top-level test areas plus the mutation/coverage/test-wrapper infra, though production src/ and plugins/ code should remain untouched (test-only refactor). db_migration=false (no schema), provider_surface=false (no chat/task-tracker adapter changes), credentials=false. novelty=existing-modules: this refactors existing test files under an established bun:test convention; it creates no new top-level module.
